title: One document harness for the clinician note, UAP, FMM and Four Horsemen
head: 3758b0901c4f85ad955e1a6f0cb02804c838147b

claims.text: The editor takes only an EditableFinding. A plain Finding or a classify result is a type error.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 9
claims.reason: V01 went red on control K01.

plain.what: The editor accepts only an `EditableFinding`. An `EditableFinding` is a finding that passed the editability gate. A raw finding is a type error.
plain.proof: Two type pins (V01, V02) and the full type check (V35). We loosened the types, and the checks went red.
plain.warning: One control (K01b) made the editor accept any input. Pin V01 stayed green. Only the full type check (V35) found it. Thus, pin V01 is weaker than it looks.

claims.text: Wiring rejects an adapter and a subset of different kinds.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 9
claims.reason: V03 went red on control K03.

plain.what: The wiring joins an adapter to its settings. A UAP adapter with FMM settings is a type error.
plain.proof: Two type pins (V03, V04). We loosened the types, and both went red.

claims.text: run_adapter and _run_kind reject an adapter, a subset or a setup of a different kind.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 9
claims.reason: V05 went red on control K05.

plain.what: `run_adapter` and `_run_kind` refuse an adapter, a subset or a setup of a different kind.
plain.proof: Two type pins (V05, V06). We loosened the types, and both went red.

claims.text: Outputs rejects the note kind, because write_outputs does not write it.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 9
claims.reason: V07 went red on control K07.

plain.what: `write_outputs` does not write notes. Thus, the type of its input does not permit the note kind.
plain.proof: One type pin (V07). We loosened the type, and it went red.

claims.text: A docgen module imports only the docgen modules that its DOCGEN_IMPORTS row lists.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 9
claims.reason: V08 went red on control K08.

plain.what: A table lists, for each docgen file, the docgen files that it can import. Other imports are not permitted.
plain.proof: The boundary check (V08). We deleted one row from the table, and the check went red.

claims.text: No adapter imports another adapter.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 9
claims.reason: V09 went red on control K09.

plain.what: The code for one kind does not use the code for a different kind.
plain.proof: The boundary check (V09). We added a bad import, and the check went red.

claims.text: The core imports no CLI, FMM, 4H, refine or cr.uap module.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 9
claims.reason: V10 went red on control K10.

plain.what: The shared loop does not import the CLI or the FMM, 4H, refine or UAP code.
plain.proof: The boundary check (V10). We added a bad import, and the check went red.

claims.text: Only clinician_note and the allowlist import cr.note.author and cr.note.loop.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 9
claims.reason: V11 went red on control K11.

plain.what: Only `clinician_note` (and files on the approved list) can import `cr.note.author` and `cr.note.loop`.
plain.proof: The boundary check (V11). We deleted one row from the approved list, and the check went red.

claims.text: Only finished_cr.py and tests/_crp_fixtures.py call FinishedCR.
claims.source: PR body, This is what we did, and section 9
claims.reason: V12 went red on control K12.

plain.what: Only `finished_cr.py` and the test fixture can make a `FinishedCR`. Thus, no code can skip the CR acceptance checks.
plain.proof: The boundary check (V12). We deleted one row from the approved list, and the check went red.

claims.text: Only findings.py calls EditableFinding.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, sections 3 and 9
claims.reason: V13 went red on control K13.

plain.what: Only `findings.py` can make an `EditableFinding`. Thus, no code can skip the editability gate.
plain.proof: The boundary check (V13). We added a bad call in a different file, and the check went red.

claims.text: The editor never gets a finding whose key is in not_editable.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 3
claims.reason: V14 went red on control K14.

plain.what: Some findings must not be repaired by editing text, for example a finding about a lab result. The judge grades them, but the editor does not see them.
plain.proof: An integration test (V14) runs the UAP adapter with a test judge. We deleted the guard line, and the test went red.

claims.text: An evidence_bound finding is editable only in a card file whose evidence holds its input fact.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 3
claims.reason: V15 went red on control K15.

plain.what: An `evidence_bound` finding is about one input fact. The editor can change only a card whose evidence holds that fact.
plain.proof: An integration test (V15). We deleted the guard line, and the test went red.

claims.text: The editor never gets a model major that the second sample did not report again.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 3
claims.reason: V16 went red on control K16.

plain.what: The judge checks the draft one time. If a model reports a major finding that no earlier round marked as blocking, the judge checks the draft again for that finding only. The editor gets the finding only when the second check reports it again.
plain.proof: An integration test (V16) gives the judge a major finding that the second check does not report again. We deleted the guard line, and the test went red.

claims.text: A second report counts only for the same claim: the cartridge, the key and the place.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 3
claims.reason: V17 went red on control K17.

plain.what: The second report counts only when it has the same cartridge, the same key and the same place. A report about a different file does not count.
plain.proof: Two integration tests (V17, V18). We deleted the code that compares the claims, and both tests went red.

claims.text: The edit rounds stop after a round that the accept rule did not keep and that changed no file.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 1, and Merge danger
claims.reason: V19 went red on control K19.

plain.what: If the accept rule refuses a round, and that round changed no file, the edit rounds stop.
plain.proof: An integration test (V19) runs the loop with a test adapter and a scripted editor. We deleted the guard line, and the test went red.

claims.text: A floor finding that no writable file holds stops the edit rounds.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 1
claims.reason: V20 went red on control K20.

plain.what: A safety-floor finding can be in a file that the editor cannot write. Then the edit rounds stop.
plain.proof: An integration test (V20). We deleted the guard line, and the test went red.

claims.text: A lost editor call never reflects or releases its partial edit.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 1
claims.reason: V21 went red on control K21.

plain.what: If an editor call stops before it is complete, its partial edit is not checked again and is not released.
plain.proof: An integration test (V21). We deleted the guard line, and the test went red.

claims.text: The finish tool refuses while a code check reports a blocking finding, up to three times.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 5
claims.reason: V22 went red on control K22.

plain.what: The finish tool refuses while a code check reports a blocking finding. It refuses a maximum of three times.
plain.proof: An integration test (V22). We reversed the condition, and the test went red.

claims.text: The editor cannot delete a writable file.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 5
claims.reason: V23 went red on control K23.

plain.what: The editor can change a file that it can write, but it cannot delete that file.
plain.proof: An integration test (V23) sends a delete command. We deleted the guard line, and the test went red.

claims.text: LastClean restores the last kept draft with no blocking finding, not the first.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 6
claims.reason: V24 went red on control K24.

plain.what: If the loop must go back, `LastClean` restores the latest kept draft that has no blocking finding.
plain.proof: An integration test (V24). We reversed the condition, and the test went red.

claims.text: The judiciary reflector refuses a worker that is not synthetic-only.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 4
claims.reason: V25 went red on control K25.

plain.what: The judiciary reflector refuses a worker that does not tell it "synthetic data only".
plain.proof: An integration test (V25) starts a test worker with 30 bad start messages. We deleted the guard line, and the test went red.

claims.text: cr docgen sends model requests that are byte-identical to the golden file.
claims.source: PR body, This is how we proved it
claims.reason: V26 went red on control K26.

plain.what: `cr docgen` sends requests to the model that are the same, byte for byte, as a saved file (the golden file).
plain.proof: A golden test (V26) compares a hash of each request with the golden file. We changed one byte in the golden file, and the test went red.

claims.text: In the 14 scripted sessions, cr docgen --kind note sends the requests of write_clinician_note.
claims.source: PR body, This is why it's better
claims.reason: V27 went red on control K27.

plain.what: In 14 scripted sessions, `cr docgen --kind note` sends the same requests as `write_clinician_note`.
plain.proof: A parity test (V27) runs each session through both paths. We deleted the code that the test covers, and the test went red.

claims.text: cr uap and cr fmm call cr docgen with --reflection none.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, section 8
claims.reason: V28 went red on control K28.

plain.what: `cr uap` and `cr fmm` call `cr docgen` with no reflection.
plain.proof: A parity test (V28) compares the requests of the old and new commands. We reversed the condition, and the test went red.

claims.text: Each kind refuses a CR that fails CR-33 acceptance.
claims.source: PR body, How it works, sections 2 and 8
claims.reason: V29 went red on control K29.

plain.what: CR-33 is the acceptance check for a CR. If a CR fails it, no kind makes a document from it.
plain.proof: An integration test (V29) runs each kind on a bad CR. We deleted the guard line, and the test went red.

claims.text: cr docgen --reflection judiciary works with the real judiciary reflection worker.
claims.source: PR body, Known issues: the real judiciary-worker e2e test skips in CI
claims.reason: Only the PR text states this claim. V36 is cannot-fail.

plain.what: `cr docgen --reflection judiciary` operates with the real judiciary worker, not only a test worker.
plain.proof: It is not proven. A test (V36) exists, but it skips when judiciary is not built. We planted a bug, and the test skipped and stayed green. Thus, the test cannot fail now.

claims.text: Against production, the CR note agent cuts agreed blind failures from 2.65 to 0.02 per note.
claims.source: PR body, This is why it's better
claims.reason: V30 backs this claim, but the evidence is recorded, not run again.

plain.what: Two blind labellers agree on failures. The rate goes down from 2.65 to 0.02 for each note.
plain.proof: A pre-registered eval (V30) on 23 test members. gpt-6.1-sol and Opus labelled each note, and they did not know which path made it. This is a record. We did not run it again.

claims.text: The harness is non-inferior to main for FMM, 4H and the UAP after the anti-gaming changes.
claims.source: PR body, This is why it's better
claims.reason: V31 backs this claim, but the evidence is recorded, not run again.

plain.what: After the anti-gaming changes, each kind is at least as good as main.
plain.proof: Frozen judges graded both paths three times on 5 members (V31). Two blind labellers also labelled each document. This is a record.
plain.warning: The UAP result uses the same 5 members that we used to tune the anti-gaming changes.

claims.text: An Opus audit found no gaming in the kept edits.
claims.source: PR body, This is how we proved it
claims.reason: V32 backs this claim, but the evidence is recorded, not run again.

plain.what: No kept edit hides a problem without a repair.
plain.proof: Opus read each kept edit (V32). This is a model opinion, not a tool check.
plain.warning: Opus is in the same model family as the author. Thus, it is not a fully independent check.

claims.text: The cost per document goes up: UAP $0.75 to $1.30, FMM $0.34 to $0.38, 4H $0.24 to $0.32.
claims.source: PR body, This is why it's better
claims.reason: V33 backs this claim, but the evidence is recorded, not run again.

plain.what: UAP goes up from $0.75 to $1.30. FMM goes up from $0.34 to $0.38. 4H goes up from $0.24 to $0.32.
plain.proof: The cost meter of each run (V33). This is a record.

claims.text: 4,249 CR tests, 1,272 harness tests and 74 root tests pass. Ruff, basedpyright and the boundary checks are clean.
claims.source: PR body, This is how we proved it
claims.reason: V34 backs this claim, but the evidence is recorded, not run again.

plain.what: 4,249 CR tests, 1,272 harness tests and 74 root tests pass. Ruff, basedpyright and the boundary checks are clean.
plain.proof: The CI jobs ran at the PR head (V34). This is a record. We did not run them again.

claims.text: Production does not change, because cr_service does not import cr.docgen.
claims.source: PR body, This is why it's better, and Merge danger
claims.reason: V37, V38 backs this claim, but it is a mechanical check (a grep or a line count) with no control.

plain.what: The production service does not import the new harness code. Thus, the new code cannot change production.
plain.proof: A grep (V37) finds no import of `cr.docgen` in the 362 files under `cr_service` at the PR head. A second grep (V38) finds that no `cr_service` file imports `cr.cli`, the only other module that imports the harness. No control ran, so the claim is Backed, not Proven.
plain.warning: A grep reads only the import lines at the head. No CI rule stops a new import after the merge.

claims.text: The source code is 47 lines smaller than main.
claims.source: PR body, This is what we did
claims.reason: V39 backs this claim, but it is a mechanical check (a grep or a line count) with no control.

plain.what: The PR deletes more source lines than it adds.
plain.proof: A line count (V39) of the diff in `src/` and `harness/src/` gives +7,017 and -7,064 lines: net -47, as the PR says.

claims.text: The UAP trace label released, on a plan that needs clinician review, is a label error and not a floor gap.
claims.source: PR body, Known issues
claims.reason: Only the PR text states this claim.

plain.what: The harness released one UAP plan with a label that needs clinician review. The PR says that the label is wrong, and that the safety floor did not fail.
plain.proof: It is not proven. A clinician must examine it.

claims.text: Nobody measured the two folded defaults, #438 and #424, in production.
claims.source: PR body, Merge danger
claims.reason: Only the PR text states this claim.

plain.what: The PR includes two default settings from PRs 438 and 424. Nobody measured them in production.
plain.proof: It is not proven. This is a statement that something is missing.

claims.text: require_same_scope refuses a packet and a ledger of different members or snapshots.
claims.source: scan: projects/clinical-reasoning/src/cr/generation_util.py changed, and no test names it. The PR text does not name require_same_scope.
claims.reason: No verifier backs this claim, and the PR text does not state it.

plain.what: `require_same_scope` refuses a packet and a ledger that are for different members or different snapshots.
plain.proof: It is not proven. No test gives it a mismatched pair.

claims.text: No caller uses sheet_names, which the PR deletes from guidance/_xlsx.py.
claims.source: scan: projects/clinical-reasoning/src/cr/guidance/_xlsx.py changed, and no test names it. The PR text does not name sheet_names.
claims.reason: No verifier backs this claim, and the PR text does not state it.

plain.what: The PR deletes `sheet_names` from `guidance/_xlsx.py`. The PR assumes that no code calls it.
plain.proof: It is not proven. A search of the repo, or the type check, would prove it.

claims.text: With diagnose, submission_text names the unexpected tool calls, not an empty body.
claims.source: scan: projects/clinical-reasoning/src/cr/generation_util.py changed, and no test names it. The PR text does not name diagnose.
claims.reason: No verifier backs this claim, and the PR text does not state it.

plain.what: When the model makes tool calls that we do not expect, `submission_text` names those calls. It does not show an empty body.
plain.proof: It is not proven. No test sends unexpected tool calls in diagnose mode.

verdict_intros.Proven: For each claim here, a tool check exists, and the check went red on a planted bug.
verdict_intros.Backed: For each claim here, evidence exists, but we did not run it again. It is a record of a past run.
verdict_intros.Asserted: For each claim here, only the PR text says it. No check proves it.
verdict_intros.Gap: For each claim here, no check exists, and the PR does not state the claim. You must decide if it is important.

promises.label: Checked input, separate lanes
promises.sentence: Only a checked CR goes into the harness, and each document kind stays in its own lane.
promises.reviewer_action: Do not trust that one document can never mix two members. No test gives the harness a record and a packet from different members.

promises.label: No gaming the Judge
promises.sentence: The editor gets only the findings that it can repair, so it cannot hide a problem from the Judge.
promises.reviewer_action: Treat the gaming audit as one opinion: an Opus model from the author's model family did it. Read the kept edits yourself, or audit them with another model family.

promises.label: Bad edits never ship
promises.sentence: A bad edit does not go out: the loop undoes it, stops, or blocks the document.
promises.reviewer_action: Ask a clinician to read the UAP plan that the trace marks released, because only the PR text says that the label is wrong.

promises.label: Same requests, working commands
promises.sentence: The harness sends the same model requests as the old code, and each command and mode still operates.
promises.reviewer_action: Judiciary mode is not verified, so do not rely on it yet: its only end-to-end test skips. Also search for callers of the deleted spreadsheet helper before you merge.

promises.label: Better notes, no production change
promises.sentence: The notes get better at a higher cost per document, the code gets smaller, and production does not change.
promises.reviewer_action: Do not expect these results in production yet. The note eval tested an earlier version of the note code, and nobody measured the two folded defaults in production.

exercises.title: Trace it: when do the edit rounds stop?
exercises.scenario: cr docgen runs the edit loop on a UAP draft. Step the draft through the end of the loop in projects/clinical-reasoning/src/cr/docgen/loop.py.

steps.prompt: Round 2: the editor finishes its session, but it changes no file. The accept rule does not keep the round. What does the loop do next?
choices: It starts round 3 from the same draft.
steps.why: _idle (loop.py:101-107) ends the rounds. Another round starts from the same draft and the same findings, so it cannot help (C15).

steps.prompt: A floor finding remains, and no writable file holds it. Can a further edit release the draft?
choices: Yes. The editor can fix it in a different file.
Yes. The judge removes the finding.
steps.why: _unfixable (loop.py:69-71) is true, so the rounds stop. No edit can release the draft (C16).

steps.prompt: The loop stops with a floor finding in the final draft. The adapter has a fallback, and the code checks find no floor finding on it. What does _floor release?
choices: The draft with the floor finding.
steps.why: _floor restores the fallback. The fallback stands because the code checks find no floor finding on it.
